key_insight: A dual-layer pipeline combining LLM-based screening with expert educator review can efficiently generate and validate synthetic musculoskeletal teaching cases, but human review is still needed to catch subtle clinical flaws.
clinical_relevance: Synthetic case generation may help expand health professional education datasets without using real patient records, while preserving plausibility and teaching utility.
method: Generated 128 synthetic MSK cases across 28 conditions using GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Llama 4 Scout.
Filtered cases with an LLM-as-judge quality screen covering alignment, JSON correctness, relevance, bias, toxicity, and completeness.
Sent 90 passing cases to four MSK physiotherapy educators for 5-point ratings of accuracy, realism, fidelity, relevance, and usability.
evidence_signal: Automated screening passed 70.3% of cases, and expert review found high content validity for usability and relevance (97.5% each) and realism (95%), with GPT-4.1 performing best overall.
watch_item: The approach showed weaker alignment between automated metrics and true clinical correctness, so reliance on automated filters alone could miss important medical inaccuracies.
paper_title: PhysiCase: Development and dual-layer validation of synthetic cases for health professional education: A pilot study leveraging Generative AI
